knowledge:
- key_parameters: folder_path=Path to the folder containing raw flow cytometry index files (.fcs) ;; compensation=Logical indicating whether to apply the compensation matrix within the index files ;; plate_wells=Number of wells in the plate (e.g., 96 or 384) ;; probe1/probe2=Channel names or custom names for the probes used during sorting ;; posvalue_probe1/posvalue_probe2=Threshold values for determining positive fluorescence/specificity ;; folder_sequences=Path to the folder containing raw Sanger sequences (.ab1) ;; secondary.peak.ratio=Ratio threshold for identifying secondary peaks ;; trim.cutoff=Probability cutoff for trimming low-quality ends of Sanger sequences ;; processor/threads=Number of processors/cores to use for parallel processing ;; database=Path to the preferred IgBlast database folder containing V, D, and J fasta files ;; fasta=Path to the input fasta file for IgBlast.
- alternatives: None mentioned. The package uses sangerseqR internally for reading ab1 files, but scifer provides the high-level integration and automated plate-level processing.
- when_to_use: Use when you have single-cell index-sorted B or T cells in 96 or 384-well plates, have sequenced them using Sanger sequencing, and want to integrate the flow cytometry marker expression/specificity with the resulting BCR/TCR sequences while performing quality control and IgBlast analysis.
- pitfalls: The nomenclature of the .fcs files and the Sanger sequence subfolders must match exactly for successful merging ;; Setting compensation incorrectly can lead to incorrect specificity assignment ;; Selecting incorrect thresholds will misclassify cell specificity ;; IgBlast requires a specific database folder structure (containing V.fasta, D.fasta, J.fasta) and may have OS-specific compatibility constraints (e.g., basilisk/conda issues on Windows/macOS ARM).

workflows.name: bcr_tcr_flow_sanger_integration
workflows.intent: Process flow cytometry index sorting data, perform quality control on Sanger sequencing files, integrate both datasets to assign specificity, and run IgBlast analysis.
input: IgBlast database folder (containing V.fasta, D.fasta, J.fasta)
workflows.stages: 1. Process flow cytometry index sorting data using fcs_processing and visualize with fcs_plot ;; 2. Summarize Sanger sequence quality using summarise_quality (or summarise_abi_file for a single file) ;; 3. Integrate flow cytometry and Sanger sequencing data and generate a quality report using quality_report ;; 4. Run IgBlast analysis on the resulting sequences using igblast.
workflows.code:
fcs_data <- fcs_processing(
    folder_path = system.file("/extdata/fcs_index_sorting", package = "scifer"),
    compensation = TRUE, plate_wells = 96,
    probe1 = "Pre.F", probe2 = "Post.F",
    posvalue_probe1 = 600, posvalue_probe2 = 400
)

fcs_plot(fcs_data)

colnames(fcs_data)

unique(fcs_data$specificity)

abi_seq <- sangerseqR::read.abif(
    system.file("/extdata/sorted_sangerseq/E18_C1/A1_3_IgG_Inner.ab1",
        package = "scifer"
    )
)

summarised <- summarise_abi_file(abi_seq)
head(summarised[["summary"]])
head(summarised[["quality_score"]])

sf <- summarise_quality(
    folder_sequences = system.file("extdata/sorted_sangerseq", package = "scifer"),
    secondary.peak.ratio = 0.33, trim.cutoff = 0.01, processor = 1
)

colnames(sf[["summaries"]])

head(sf[["summaries"]][4:10])

quality_report(
    folder_sequences = system.file("extdata/sorted_sangerseq", package = "scifer"),
    outputfile = "QC_report.html", output_dir = "~/full/path/to/your/location",
    folder_path_fcs = system.file("extdata/fcs_index_sorting",
        package = "scifer"
    ),
    probe1 = "Pre.F", probe2 = "Post.F",
    posvalue_probe1 = 600, posvalue_probe2 = 400
)

ighv_res <- igblast(
        database = system.file("/extdata/test_fasta/KIMDB_rm", package = "scifer"),
        fasta = system.file("/extdata/test_fasta/test_igblast.txt", package = "scifer"),
        threads = 1
)

head(ighv_res, 2)
